candidate.answerReason: The solutions are -b/a and -b'/a'. Multiplying their strict comparison by -1 reverses the inequality and yields b'/a' < b/a.

methods.label: Compare the two solutions directly
methods.explanation:
Since \(a\ne0\) and \(a'\ne0\), the equations have the unique solutions
\[
x=-\frac ba
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
x=-\frac{b'}{a'}.
\]
The first solution is smaller exactly when
\[
-\frac ba<-\frac{b'}{a'}.
\]
Multiplying both sides by \(-1\) reverses the inequality, giving
\[
\frac{b'}{a'}<\frac ba.
\]
Every step is reversible, so this is an if-and-only-if condition. It works for either sign of \(a\) and \(a'\). The answer is choice E.
